summary: Customer sidecar logging flood in dedicated pool leads to GPU attach timeouts and autoscaler stalls
description:
Issue summary:
ParcelAI reported a sharp midday throughput degradation in their dedicated GPU pool. Requests started queueing and p99 latency spiked; many requests ended with 504 / attach-timeout errors. Customer-facing routes using gptx-13b-v0.9 were most affected.

Impact:
- ~40% drop in throughput for ParcelAI tenant between 11:40-12:30 PDT, causing user-facing timeouts.
- Multiple GPU attach failures and allocator retries observed; autoscaler did not trigger additional capacity rapidly.
- Other tenants on the same reserved cluster saw mild p50 rise but not full outage.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: reserved-cluster rsv-wn-27 in us-west-2
- Customer: ParcelAI (dedicated contract)
- Model: gptx-13b-v0.9 pinned

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Send sustained chat load using parallel short-stream requests (avg length 60 tokens) to ParcelAI tenant routes.
2) Observe request latency and error rate around midday traffic burst.

Observed behavior:
- Autoscaler remained at baseline capacity for ~8 minutes while attachments failed with repeated timeouts.
- Sidecar logs (ParcelAI's sidecar) show a sustained flood of DEBUG/TRACE entries that coincided with the window; average socket queue length for the sidecar process increased.
- Kernel-level NIC transmit queue length and connection backlog on the node spiked, per node metrics.
- Allocator logs show repeated "gpu attach timeout" entries and incremental backoff attempts.

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler should detect capacity pressure and provision extra nodes promptly; attach timeouts should be limited and retried without causing widespread request failures.

Logs / metrics collected:
- Grafana dashboards: d/cluster/dedicated-rsv-wn-27 (p95 latency, attach-failures, node-net-queue)
- Sample allocator errors from 2026-03-12T18:41:12Z: "ATTACH_TIMEOUT tenant=parcelai request_id=..."
- Sidecar logfile snippet: "2026-03-12T18:40:23Z DEBUG http: received verbose trace - payload size=12kb" repeated thousands of times
- Node-level nic stats: tx_queue_length spiked to 512 (baseline 16)
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: noisy tenant traffic causing GPU slot starvation.
Findings after first-pass triage:
- Noise source traced to customer's sidecar; debugging flags had been enabled earlier that morning during a customer troubleshooting session. The sidecar emitted verbose traces and periodic healthcheck bursts (high-frequency keepalive + large diagnostics blobs).
- The sidecar logging flood saturated the host NIC and increased system call overhead, which delayed scheduler heartbeats and allocator attach handshakes. This caused attach timeouts even though raw GPU memory usage was below thresholds.
- Autoscaler decision loop uses only queue/attach-failure counts and CPU/memory signals; it did not consider host network saturation as a trigger, so scale-up was slower than required.
- Affected nodes were not being cordoned, so allocator retries compounded and caused slot contention for ~8 minutes.
Evidence and artifacts:
- Correlated spike in sidecar debug logs with first attach timeout at 2026-03-12T18:40:45Z.
- Node metrics: net.core.somaxconn and tcp_max_syn_backlog were exhausted on 3/5 nodes in the shard.
- Related internal alarm: INT-3321 created to track autoscaler enhancement to include node network backpressure metrics.

Temporary mitigation performed:
1) Requested ParcelAI to switch their sidecar logging to INFO via admin toggle (applied at 18:47Z).
2) Manually increased autoscaler target (min_replicas +2) for the reserved cluster at 18:50Z to buy headroom.
3) Rolled restart of sidecar processes across affected nodes to clear socket backlog at 18:55Z.

Result: throughput returned to expected baseline within ~6 minutes of toggling logs and autoscaler bump. No data loss reported.

Root cause hypothesis: customer sidecar generated a high-volume diagnostic logging flood that caused host-level network saturation and system-call pressure, which in turn triggered allocator attach timeouts and prevented the autoscaler from reacting fast enough. Autoscaler logic lacking network-backpressure signals allowed a delayed scale response.
comments: Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-12 18:48Z: Received alert from ParcelAI support channel about p99 > 12s and 504s. Opened ticket and collected initial logs. Asked customer to confirm any recent config changes.

Customer (ParcelAI - Elena Ruiz) 2026-03-12 18:52Z: We enabled verbose sidecar logging at 10:00 PDT to troubleshoot a separate model output issue. We didn't expect production impact. Happy to roll back if needed.

SRE (Arjun Patel) 2026-03-12 18:56Z: Observed repeated ATTACH_TIMEOUT in allocator logs and node nic backlog. Temporarily bumped autoscaler min_replicas and requested customer switch logs to INFO. Taking over coordination for remediation.
Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-12 19:00Z: ParcelAI confirmed logging level reverted to INFO. Performing rolling restart of sidecar workers on 3 affected nodes now.

SRE (Arjun Patel) 2026-03-12 19:06Z: Rolling restart completed. Observed drop in socket queue and attach timeouts stopped. Autoscaler scaled to manual target and then normalized. Marking incident as mitigated. Follow-up engineering work required.
Customer (Elena Ruiz) 2026-03-12 19:12Z: Thanks team — latency is back to normal. We'll avoid enabling verbose logs on production sidecars without coordinating.
Product (Lila Sorensen) 2026-03-13 09:20Z: Flagging this for product backlog: consider allowing per-tenant logging rate limits and autoscaler to ingest node net metrics. Raised INT-3321 for tracking.

SRE (Arjun Patel) 2026-03-13 11:03Z: Postmortem notes: create automated alert for sustained sidecar log throughput > 100MB/min and add autoscaler heuristic to include node net queue and attach-failure over short window.
resolution_notes:
Short-term fixes applied:
- Instructed ParcelAI to set sidecar logging to INFO (client-side change).
- Manually increased autoscaler min_replicas for the affected reserved cluster to provide immediate capacity.
- Performed rolling restart of sidecar processes to clear socket backlogs.

Long-term actions (tracked in INT-3321):
- Autoscaler enhancement to consider host-level network backpressure (net_queue_len, socket_backlog) and attach-failure spike patterns. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/891)
- Implement per-tenant sidecar logging throttle and admin guardrails to prevent verbose logging in production reserved pools.
- Add alert rule: sidecar_log_bytes_per_min > 100MB for 2m -> page oncall and throttle logs automatically.
- Update runbook: dedicated-pool noisy-sidecar -> steps for customer outreach, autoscaler manual override, and graceful restart procedure.

Ticket closed after customer confirmation and monitoring window of 2 hours with stable metrics.
